summary: Ai-Ais Airport is a small remote airstrip in the ǁKaras Region of southern Namibia, serving the Ai-Ais Hot Springs Resort and providing access to the nearby Fish River Canyon, one of Africa's largest canyons. The airport primarily handles charter and tourist flights connecting visitors to this isolated desert destination. Its location makes it a vital gateway for travelers exploring Namibia's dramatic southern landscapes.
faqs:
Q: What is Ai-Ais Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport mainly serves tourist and charter flights heading to the Ai-Ais Hot Springs Resort and Fish River Canyon area.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Ai-Ais Airport?
A: No scheduled commercial services operate; visitors typically arrange charter or fly-in safari packages through tour operators.

Q: What attractions are near Ai-Ais Airport?
A: The Fish River Canyon, Ai-Ais Hot Springs, and the Ai-Ais/Richtersveld Transfrontier Park are all within reach of the airstrip.

Q: Is the airport suitable for large aircraft?
A: No, it is a small unpaved airstrip suitable only for light aircraft and small charter planes.
transport_tips: Ground transport must be pre-arranged, as there are no taxis or public transport at the airport. Most visitors are met by lodge or safari vehicle transfers from the Ai-Ais Hot Springs Resort or tour operators. Rental cars are not available on-site, so booking a fly-in safari package that includes transfers is the most practical option.
local_tip: Pack a swimsuit in your carry-on — the Ai-Ais Hot Springs are just a short drive from the airstrip, and many visitors head straight for a relaxing soak upon arrival after the dusty journey.
